summary.text: A 63-year-old man with hypertension and hyperlipidemia, and no diabetes or chronic kidney disease, was referred to the authors' hospital for epigastric pain and recurrent gastric ulcers of undetermined cause. Five years earlier an upper endoscopy for persistent severe epigastric pain showed multiple erosions and ulcers; biopsy showed only inflammatory findings, he was Helicobacter pylori antibody negative and used no NSAIDs or anti-thrombotics, and the mucosa improved with proton pump inhibitors.

Upper endoscopy with gastric dilatation by air insufflation showed the gastric mucosa turning white in patches over time, and biopsy from the white mucosa showed no specific findings. Aortic CT on the same day showed complete occlusion of the superior mesenteric artery and stenosis of the celiac artery, attributed to atherosclerosis, and chronic ischemic gastritis was diagnosed.

He had no obvious organ ischemia, with blood flow maintained through the inferior mesenteric artery, and was followed as an outpatient with abdominal pain after eating. Because of recurrent pain and the risk of organ ischemia, a surgical bypass using the right great saphenous vein was performed two weeks after diagnosis. Postoperative endoscopy showed no mucosal color change even with gastric dilatation, and the patient no longer had abdominal pain.

article_limitations: Caption-layer visual status is not_inspected; the actual images are inspected in the separate visual submission.
No calendar dates are printed; timing is relative only (five years earlier, same day, two weeks after diagnosis).
Table 1 lists published literature reports and is not patient data; the discussion statements about CIG in the literature are not patient facts.

Video S1 (supplement deo2192-supitem-0001) is cited in the text for the endoscopic whitening; it is reviewed in the supplement manifest by sampled frames and no clinical fact is taken from it. The empty supplement entry deo2192-supinfo-0001 has no declared asset.
The mucosal color change is described by the authors as occurring with gastric dilatation; the discussion causes are hypotheses and are not recorded as asserted causes.
Whether the discussion sentence about no white mucosal development once the stomach was fully dilated refers to the endoscopy at diagnosis or after surgery is not stated; it is kept as an ambiguity.
The proton pump inhibitor course has no stated time and is not ordered against the other events.
